one of the acts in sub-section (2)(a)-(e) -- selling/hiring/distributing/exhibiting/circulating/producing/possessing for those purposes, importing/exporting/conveying, profiting from such a business, advertising such material or services, or attempting any of the above
first conviction: up to two years plus fine up to five thousand rupees; second or subsequent conviction: up to five years plus fine up to ten thousand rupees
exceptions_and_qualifications: Does not extend to material whose publication is proved justified as being for the public good on grounds of science, literature, art, learning, or other objects of general concern, or kept/used bona fide for religious purposes.

Does not extend to representations on ancient monuments (under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958) or on temples/idol-conveyance cars kept or used for religious purposes.
breakdown.how_to_read: The sub-section (1) obscenity test ('taken as a whole,' likely-audience-focused) is the threshold question that must be answered before any of the sub-section (2) conduct limbs can apply; always check the Exception next -- genuine scientific, literary, artistic, or bona fide religious material is carved out even if it might otherwise satisfy the obscenity test.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: उपधारा (1) 'अश्लील' की परिभाषा देती है। उपधारा (2) अश्लील पुस्तकों, चित्रों आदि की बिक्री, वितरण, प्रदर्शनी, आयात-निर्यात आदि से संबंधित विस्तृत आचरण को अपराध बनाती है, जिसमें बार-बार दोषसिद्धि पर दंड बढ़ता जाता है। दो अपवाद हैं — लोकहित/वैज्ञानिक-साहित्यिक-कलात्मक औचित्य, तथा प्राचीन स्मारकों/सद्भावी धार्मिक उपयोग से संबंधित वस्तुएं।
essential_elements_hi: उपधारा (1) के परीक्षण के अर्थ में कोई वस्तु अश्लील होना (कामोत्तेजक, कामुक आकर्षण वाली, या समग्र रूप से संभावित पाठकों/दर्शकों/श्रोताओं को भ्रष्ट/पथभ्रष्ट करने वाली प्रवृत्ति)

उपधारा (2)(क)-(ङ) में वर्णित किसी कार्य को करना — बेचना/किराये पर देना/वितरित करना/प्रदर्शित करना/प्रसारित करना/उत्पादन करना/उन प्रयोजनों हेतु कब्जे में रखना, आयात/निर्यात/परिवहन करना, ऐसे व्यवसाय से लाभ कमाना, ऐसी वस्तु या सेवा का विज्ञापन करना, या उपर्युक्त में से किसी का प्रयत्न करना
प्रथम दोषसिद्धि पर: दो वर्ष तक व पाँच हजार रुपये तक जुर्माना; द्वितीय या पश्चातवर्ती दोषसिद्धि पर: पाँच वर्ष तक व दस हजार रुपये तक जुर्माना
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: लोकहित हेतु न्यायोचित प्रकाशन, जैसे विज्ञान, साहित्य, कला या सीखने के उद्देश्य से उचित प्रमाणित वस्तुएं
प्राचीन स्मारक पर उत्कीर्ण या रखी गई वस्तुएं, या सद्भावी धार्मिक प्रयोजन हेतु प्रयुक्त वस्तुएं
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: पहले परिभाषा पढ़ें, फिर अपराधकारी आचरण की व्यापक सूची, और अंत में दोनों अपवादों की जाँच करें, क्योंकि ये अभियोजन को पूर्णतः निरस्त कर सकते हैं।

sections.title: Sale, etc., of obscene objects to child
sections.raw_text: Whoever sells, lets to hire, distributes, exhibits or circulates to any child any such obscene object as is referred to in section 294, or offers or attempts so to do, shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, and, in the event of a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and also with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
key_terms: selling or distributing an obscene object to a child

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 295 BNS is the child-protection escalation of Section 294 -- selling, hiring, distributing, exhibiting, or circulating (or attempting to do any of these with) an obscene object as defined in Section 294, specifically to a child, carrying heavier punishment than the general obscenity offence: up to three years on first conviction, up to seven years on repeat conviction.
essential_elements: an object that qualifies as obscene under Section 294's definition
selling, letting to hire, distributing, exhibiting, or circulating that object to a child, or offering/attempting to do so
first conviction: up to three years plus fine up to two thousand rupees; second or subsequent conviction: up to seven years plus fine up to five thousand rupees
breakdown.how_to_read: Compare directly against Section 294: the imprisonment maximum here is higher at every tier (3 years vs. 2 years on first conviction; 7 years vs. 5 years on repeat) despite a lower first-conviction fine ceiling, reflecting the heightened seriousness the Sanhita attaches to exposing children specifically to obscene material.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: यह धारा 294 का ही बाल-संरक्षण हेतु कठोरीकृत रूप है — जब अश्लील वस्तुएं किसी बालक को बेची, किराये पर दी, वितरित की या प्रदर्शित की जाती हैं, तो प्रत्येक दंड-स्तर पर सामान्य धारा 294 की अपेक्षा अधिक कठोर दंड लागू होता है।
essential_elements_hi: धारा 294(1) के अर्थ में अश्लील वस्तु होना
उसे किसी बालक को बेचना, किराये पर देना, वितरित करना या अन्यथा उपलब्ध कराना
धारा 294 की तुलना में प्रत्येक दोषसिद्धि-स्तर पर कठोर दंड
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: इसे सदैव धारा 294 के साथ तुलनात्मक रूप से पढ़ें — तत्व वही हैं, केवल पीड़ित बालक होने तथा दंड कठोरतर होने में अंतर है।

sections.title: Obscene acts and songs
sections.raw_text:
Whoever, to the annoyance of others,--

(a) does any obscene act in any public place; or

(b) sings, recites or utters any obscene song, ballad or words, in or near any public place,

shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
key_terms: obscene act in a public place
obscene song ballad or words in or near a public place

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 296 BNS targets live obscene conduct in public, as distinct from Section 294's obscene-material offences -- doing an obscene act in a public place, or singing/reciting/uttering obscene songs, ballads, or words in or near a public place, to the annoyance of others, punishable with up to three months plus fine up to one thousand rupees.
essential_elements: an obscene act in a public place, OR obscene song/ballad/words sung, recited, or uttered in or near a public place
the conduct is to the annoyance of others
breakdown.how_to_read: The 'to the annoyance of others' requirement is an operative element, not mere surplus language -- the prosecution must show the conduct actually annoyed someone, tying this offence conceptually back to the public-nuisance framework opening the chapter even though it sits in the obscenity cluster.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: यह धारा जीवंत सार्वजनिक अश्लील आचरण — जैसे अश्लील कार्य करना या अश्लील गीत गाना — को दंडनीय बनाती है, जो धारा 294 की वस्तु-आधारित अपराधों से भिन्न है। अपराध पूर्ण होने हेतु यह आवश्यक है कि यह आचरण 'अन्य व्यक्तियों को क्षुब्ध करने वाला' हो।
essential_elements_hi: सार्वजनिक स्थान के निकट या उसमें अश्लील कार्य करना, या अश्लील गीत, गाथा या शब्द गाना/बोलना
ऐसा आचरण अन्य व्यक्तियों को क्षुब्ध करने वाला होना
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: ध्यान दें कि 'अन्य व्यक्तियों की क्षुब्धता' एक अनिवार्य संघटक तत्व है, न कि केवल एक परिस्थिति — इसके अभाव में अपराध सिद्ध नहीं होता।

sections.title: Keeping lottery office
sections.raw_text:
(1) Whoever keeps any office or place for the purpose of drawing any lottery not being a State lottery or a lottery authorised by the State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

(2) Whoever publishes any proposal to pay any sum, or to deliver any goods, or to do or forbear from doing anything for the benefit of any person, on any event or contingency relative or applicable to the drawing of any ticket, lot, number or figure in any such lottery, shall be punished with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
key_terms: keeping an office for an unauthorised lottery
publishing a proposal tied to the drawing of an unauthorised lottery

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 297 BNS, closing Chapter XV, targets unauthorised lotteries -- keeping an office or place for drawing any lottery that is not a State lottery or a State-Government-authorised lottery (sub-section (1)), and separately, publishing any proposal to pay money, deliver goods, or do/forbear from doing anything contingent on such an unauthorised lottery's drawing (sub-section (2)).
essential_elements: sub-section (1): keeping an office or place for the purpose of drawing a lottery that is neither a State lottery nor one authorised by the State Government

sub-section (2): publishing a proposal to pay a sum, deliver goods, or do/forbear from doing anything for a person's benefit, contingent on the drawing of a ticket, lot, number, or figure in such an unauthorised lottery
exceptions_and_qualifications: State lotteries and lotteries authorised by the State Government fall outside sub-section (1)'s prohibition entirely.
breakdown.how_to_read: The two sub-sections target different points in the unauthorised-lottery chain -- sub-section (1) the operator who keeps the drawing office (imprisonment-eligible), sub-section (2) anyone who publishes lottery-contingent proposals, such as promoters or advertisers (fine-only) -- and both carve out State-run or State-authorised lotteries from the outset.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 297 बीएनएस, अध्याय XV को बंद करते हुए, अनधिकृत लॉटरी को लक्षित करती है — किसी ऐसी लॉटरी के निकालने हेतु कार्यालय या स्थान रखना जो न तो राज्य-लॉटरी है और न ही राज्य सरकार द्वारा प्राधिकृत (उपधारा (1)), तथा पृथक रूप से, ऐसी अनधिकृत लॉटरी के टिकट/लॉट/संख्या/अंक निकाले जाने से संबंधित किसी घटना पर धन देने, माल देने या कुछ करने/न करने का प्रस्ताव प्रकाशित करना (उपधारा (2))।
essential_elements_hi: उपधारा (1): किसी ऐसी लॉटरी के निकालने हेतु कार्यालय या स्थान रखना जो न तो राज्य-लॉटरी है और न ही राज्य सरकार द्वारा प्राधिकृत
उपधारा (2): किसी ऐसी अनधिकृत लॉटरी में टिकट, लॉट, संख्या या अंक निकाले जाने पर आश्रित किसी व्यक्ति के लाभ हेतु धन देने, माल देने या कुछ करने/न करने का प्रस्ताव प्रकाशित करना
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: राज्य-लॉटरी और राज्य सरकार द्वारा प्राधिकृत लॉटरी उपधारा (1) के निषेध से पूर्णतः बाहर हैं।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: दोनों उपधाराएं अनधिकृत-लॉटरी शृंखला के भिन्न बिंदुओं को लक्षित करती हैं — उपधारा (1) निकालने का कार्यालय रखने वाले संचालक को (कारावास-योग्य), उपधारा (2) ऐसे प्रस्ताव प्रकाशित करने वाले किसी भी व्यक्ति, जैसे प्रवर्तक या विज्ञापनदाता को (केवल जुर्माना) — और दोनों आरंभ से ही राज्य-संचालित या राज्य-प्राधिकृत लॉटरी को बाहर रखती हैं।

sections.title: Injuring or defiling place of worship with intent to insult religion of any class
sections.raw_text: Whoever destroys, damages or defiles any place of worship, or any object held sacred by any class of persons with the intention of thereby insulting the religion of any class of persons or with the knowledge that any class of persons is likely to consider such destruction, damage or defilement as an insult to their religion, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
key_terms: destroying damaging or defiling a place of worship or sacred object with intent to insult religion

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 298 BNS, opening Chapter XVI, criminalises destroying, damaging, or defiling a place of worship or an object held sacred by any class of persons, where done with the intention of insulting that class's religion, or with knowledge that the class is likely to consider the act an insult to their religion, punishable with up to two years' imprisonment, fine, or both.
essential_elements: destroying, damaging, or defiling a place of worship, or an object held sacred by any class of persons
intention of thereby insulting the religion of any class of persons, OR knowledge that the class is likely to consider the act an insult to their religion
breakdown.how_to_read: The knowledge-based alternative (knowing the class is likely to view it as an insult) means this offence does not require proof of a specifically anti-religious motive -- reckless disregard for the foreseeable religious-insult impact of destroying a sacred place/object suffices just as much as deliberate intent to insult.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 298 बीएनएस, अध्याय XVI का आरंभ करते हुए, किसी पूजा स्थल या किसी वर्ग द्वारा पवित्र माने जाने वाली वस्तु को नष्ट करना, क्षति पहुँचाना या अपवित्र करना अपराध बनाती है, जहाँ यह उस वर्ग के धर्म का अपमान करने के आशय से किया जाए, या यह जानते हुए किया जाए कि वह वर्ग इसे अपने धर्म का अपमान मानने की संभावना रखता है — दो वर्ष तक के कारावास, जुर्माने या दोनों से दंडनीय।
essential_elements_hi: किसी पूजा स्थल, या किसी वर्ग द्वारा पवित्र मानी जाने वाली वस्तु को नष्ट करना, क्षति पहुँचाना या अपवित्र करना
उस वर्ग के धर्म का अपमान करने का आशय होना, अथवा यह जानते हुए कि वह वर्ग इसे अपमान मानने की संभावना रखता है
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: ज्ञान-आधारित विकल्प (यह जानना कि वह वर्ग इसे अपमान मान सकता है) का अर्थ है कि इस अपराध हेतु विशेष रूप से धर्म-विरोधी उद्देश्य सिद्ध करना आवश्यक नहीं — पवित्र स्थल/वस्तु को नष्ट करने के पूर्वानुमेय धार्मिक-अपमान प्रभाव के प्रति उपेक्षापूर्ण लापरवाही भी उतनी ही पर्याप्त है जितना जानबूझकर अपमान का आशय।

sections.title: Deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs
sections.raw_text: Whoever, with deliberate and malicious intention of outraging the religious feelings of any class of citizens of India, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representations or through electronic means or otherwise, insults or attempts to insult the religion or the religious beliefs of that class, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
key_terms: deliberate and malicious intention to outrage religious feelings
insulting religion or religious beliefs through words signs visible representations or electronic means

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 299 BNS is the Sanhita's central 'hurting religious sentiments' offence -- insulting, or attempting to insult, the religion or religious beliefs of any class of Indian citizens, by spoken or written words, signs, visible representations, or electronic means, done with deliberate and malicious intent to outrage that class's religious feelings, punishable with up to three years' imprisonment, fine, or both.
essential_elements: deliberate and malicious intention of outraging the religious feelings of a class of citizens of India
insulting or attempting to insult the religion or religious beliefs of that class
by words (spoken or written), signs, visible representations, electronic means, or otherwise
breakdown.how_to_read: The 'deliberate and malicious intention' threshold (a demanding mens rea distinct from Section 298's lower knowledge-based alternative) is the single most litigated phrase in this provision -- it requires more than merely giving offence; the intent must be to outrage religious feelings specifically, which is why courts scrutinise this element closely before allowing prosecutions to proceed, especially against artistic, academic, or satirical expression.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 299 बीएनएस संहिता की केंद्रीय 'धार्मिक भावनाओं को आहत करने' वाली धारा है — भारत के किसी वर्ग के नागरिकों की धार्मिक भावनाओं को क्षुब्ध करने के जानबूझकर व द्वेषपूर्ण आशय से, बोले या लिखे गए शब्दों, संकेतों, दृश्य निरूपणों या इलेक्ट्रॉनिक माध्यमों से उस वर्ग के धर्म या धार्मिक विश्वासों का अपमान करना या अपमान करने का प्रयत्न करना — तीन वर्ष तक के कारावास, जुर्माने या दोनों से दंडनीय।
essential_elements_hi: भारत के किसी वर्ग नागरिकों की धार्मिक भावनाओं को क्षुब्ध करने का जानबूझकर व द्वेषपूर्ण आशय
उस वर्ग के धर्म या धार्मिक विश्वासों का अपमान करना या अपमान करने का प्रयत्न करना
बोले या लिखे गए शब्दों, संकेतों, दृश्य निरूपणों, इलेक्ट्रॉनिक माध्यमों या अन्यथा के द्वारा
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: 'जानबूझकर व द्वेषपूर्ण आशय' की सीमा (धारा 298 के निम्नतर ज्ञान-आधारित विकल्प से भिन्न एक कठोर मानसिक-अवस्था अपेक्षा) इस उपबंध का सर्वाधिक विवादित वाक्यांश है — इसके लिए केवल आपत्ति उत्पन्न करना पर्याप्त नहीं; आशय विशेष रूप से धार्मिक भावनाओं को क्षुब्ध करने का होना चाहिए, इसीलिए न्यायालय अभियोजन, विशेषतः कलात्मक, शैक्षणिक या व्यंग्यात्मक अभिव्यक्ति के विरुद्ध, आगे बढ़ाने से पहले इस तत्व की बारीकी से जाँच करते हैं।

sections.title: Disturbing religious assembly
sections.raw_text: Whoever voluntarily causes disturbance to any assembly lawfully engaged in the performance of religious worship, or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
key_terms: voluntarily disturbing a lawful religious assembly

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 300 BNS protects the orderly conduct of religious worship and ceremonies -- voluntarily causing disturbance to any assembly lawfully engaged in religious worship or ceremonies, punishable with up to one year's imprisonment, fine, or both.
essential_elements: voluntarily causing disturbance
to an assembly lawfully engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies
breakdown.how_to_read: 'Lawfully engaged' is a qualifying element -- the assembly's religious activity must itself be lawful for this protection to apply, distinguishing protected worship/ceremony from unlawful assemblies that happen to have a religious character.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 300 बीएनएस धार्मिक उपासना और समारोहों के व्यवस्थित संचालन की रक्षा करती है — धार्मिक उपासना या धार्मिक समारोहों में विधिपूर्वक संलग्न किसी सभा में स्वेच्छा से विघ्न डालना, एक वर्ष तक के कारावास, जुर्माने या दोनों से दंडनीय।
essential_elements_hi: स्वेच्छा से विघ्न उत्पन्न करना
धार्मिक उपासना या धार्मिक समारोहों में विधिपूर्वक संलग्न किसी सभा में
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: 'विधिपूर्वक संलग्न' एक अर्हकारी तत्व है — इस संरक्षण के लागू होने हेतु सभा की धार्मिक गतिविधि स्वयं वैध होनी चाहिए, जो संरक्षित उपासना/समारोह को उन गैरकानूनी जमावड़ों से अलग करता है जिनमें संयोगवश धार्मिक स्वरूप हो।

sections.title: Trespassing on burial places, etc.
sections.raw_text: Whoever, with the intention of wounding the feelings of any person, or of insulting the religion of any person, or with the knowledge that the feelings of any person are likely to be wounded, or that the religion of any person is likely to be insulted thereby, commits any trespass in any place of worship or on any place of sepulchre, or any place set apart for the performance of funeral rites or as a depository for the remains of the dead, or offers any indignity to any human corpse, or causes disturbance to any persons assembled for the performance of funeral ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
key_terms: trespassing on a place of worship sepulchre or funeral site with intent to wound feelings or insult religion
offering indignity to a human corpse
disturbing persons assembled for funeral ceremonies

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 301 BNS protects places and rituals of death and burial -- trespassing in a place of worship, sepulchre, or place set apart for funeral rites/remains, offering indignity to a human corpse, or disturbing persons assembled for funeral ceremonies, where done to wound feelings or insult religion (or with knowledge that such wounding/insult is likely), punishable with up to one year's imprisonment, fine, or both.
essential_elements: intention of wounding any person's feelings, or of insulting any person's religion, OR knowledge that feelings are likely to be wounded or religion likely to be insulted

and one of: committing trespass in a place of worship or a place of sepulchre/funeral rites/remains-depository, OR offering indignity to a human corpse, OR causing disturbance to persons assembled for funeral ceremonies
breakdown.how_to_read: This section bundles three distinct physical acts (trespass on sacred/funeral sites, indignity to a corpse, disturbing a funeral assembly) under a single shared mental-state requirement -- any one of the three acts, combined with the intent/knowledge element, completes the offence.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 301 बीएनएस मृत्यु और दफन से संबंधित स्थलों व अनुष्ठानों की रक्षा करती है — किसी पूजा स्थल, कब्रिस्तान, या अंतिम संस्कार/अवशेष-निक्षेप हेतु निर्धारित स्थान में अतिचार करना, किसी मानव शव का अनादर करना, या अंतिम संस्कार में एकत्रित व्यक्तियों में विघ्न डालना, जहाँ यह किसी के भावनाओं को आहत करने या धर्म का अपमान करने हेतु किया जाए (या यह जानते हुए कि ऐसा होने की संभावना है) — एक वर्ष तक के कारावास, जुर्माने या दोनों से दंडनीय।
essential_elements_hi: किसी व्यक्ति की भावनाओं को आहत करने या धर्म का अपमान करने का आशय, अथवा यह जानते हुए कि भावनाएं आहत होने या धर्म अपमानित होने की संभावना है
और निम्न में से एक: पूजा स्थल या कब्रिस्तान/अंतिम संस्कार/अवशेष-निक्षेप स्थान में अतिचार करना, अथवा मानव शव का अनादर करना, अथवा अंतिम संस्कार में एकत्रित व्यक्तियों में विघ्न डालना
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: यह धारा तीन भिन्न भौतिक कार्यों (पवित्र/अंतिम-संस्कार स्थलों में अतिचार, शव का अनादर, अंतिम संस्कार सभा में विघ्न) को एक साझा मानसिक-अवस्था अपेक्षा के अंतर्गत जोड़ती है — तीनों में से कोई भी कार्य, आशय/ज्ञान तत्व के साथ मिलकर, अपराध को पूर्ण कर देता है।

sections.title: Uttering words, etc., with deliberate intent to wound religious feelings of any person
sections.raw_text: Whoever, with the deliberate intention of wounding the religious feelings of any person, utters any word or makes any sound in the hearing of that person or makes any gesture in the sight of that person or places any object in the sight of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
key_terms: uttering words or making sounds gestures or objects with deliberate intent to wound religious feelings

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 302 BNS, closing Chapter XVI, is the individual-targeted sibling of Section 299's class-wide offence -- with deliberate intent to wound the religious feelings of a specific person, uttering a word, making a sound in their hearing, making a gesture in their sight, or placing an object in their sight, punishable with up to one year's imprisonment, fine, or both.
essential_elements: deliberate intention of wounding the religious feelings of a specific person
uttering a word, OR making a sound in that person's hearing, OR making a gesture in that person's sight, OR placing an object in that person's sight
breakdown.how_to_read: Contrast directly with Section 299: that section protects a 'class of citizens' collectively and carries up to three years, while Section 302 protects an individual 'person' and caps at one year -- the Sanhita treats outraging a class's religious feelings as markedly graver than wounding one individual's.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 302 बीएनएस, अध्याय XVI को बंद करते हुए, धारा 299 के वर्ग-व्यापी अपराध की व्यक्ति-लक्षित प्रतिरूप है — किसी विशिष्ट व्यक्ति की धार्मिक भावनाओं को आहत करने के जानबूझकर आशय से, उसकी श्रवण-सीमा में शब्द बोलना या ध्वनि करना, उसकी दृष्टि-सीमा में संकेत करना, या उसकी दृष्टि-सीमा में कोई वस्तु रखना — एक वर्ष तक के कारावास, जुर्माने या दोनों से दंडनीय।
essential_elements_hi: किसी विशिष्ट व्यक्ति की धार्मिक भावनाओं को आहत करने का जानबूझकर आशय
कोई शब्द बोलना, अथवा उस व्यक्ति की श्रवण-सीमा में ध्वनि करना, अथवा उसकी दृष्टि-सीमा में संकेत करना, अथवा उसकी दृष्टि-सीमा में कोई वस्तु रखना
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: धारा 299 से सीधे तुलना करें: वह धारा 'नागरिकों के वर्ग' को सामूहिक रूप से संरक्षित करती है और तीन वर्ष तक दंड देती है, जबकि धारा 302 एक व्यक्ति 'person' को संरक्षित करती है और अधिकतम एक वर्ष — संहिता किसी वर्ग की धार्मिक भावनाओं को क्षुब्ध करना एक व्यक्ति की भावनाओं को आहत करने से कहीं अधिक गंभीर मानती है।

sections.title: Theft
sections.raw_text:
(1) Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.

Explanation 1.--A thing so long as it is attached to the earth, not being movable property, is not the subject of theft; but it becomes capable of being the subject of theft as soon as it is severed from the earth.

Explanation 2.--A moving effected by the same act which affects the severance may be a theft.

Explanation 3.--A person is said to cause a thing to move by removing an obstacle which prevented it from moving or by separating it from any other thing, as well as by actually moving it.

Explanation 4.--A person, who by any means causes an animal to move, is said to move that animal, and to move everything which, in consequence of the motion so caused, is moved by that animal.

Explanation 5.--The consent mentioned in this section may be express or implied, and may be given either by the person in possession, or by any person having for that purpose authority either express or implied.

Illustrations.

(a) A cuts down a tree on Z's ground, with the intention of dishonestly taking the tree out of Z's possession without Z's consent. Here, as soon as A has severed the tree in order to such taking, he has committed theft.

(b) A puts a bait for dogs in his pocket, and thus induces Z's dog to follow it. Here, if A's intention be dishonestly to take the dog out of Z's possession without Z's consent. A has committed theft as soon as Z's dog has begun to follow A.

(c) A meets a bullock carrying a box of treasure. He drives the bullock in a certain direction, in order that he may dishonestly take the treasure. As soon as the bullock begins to move, A has committed theft of the treasure.

(d) A being Z's servant, and entrusted by Z with the care of Z's plate, dishonestly runs away with the plate, without Z's consent. A has committed theft.

(e) Z, going on a journey, entrusts his plate to A, the keeper of a warehouse, till Z shall return. A carries the plate to a goldsmith and sells it. Here the plate was not in Z's possession. It could not therefore be taken out of Z's possession, and A has not committed theft, though he may have committed criminal breach of trust.

(f) A finds a ring belonging to Z on a table in the house which Z occupies. Here the ring is in Z's possession, and if A dishonestly removes it, A commits theft.

(g) A finds a ring lying on the highroad, not in the possession of any person. A, by taking it, commits no theft, though he may commit criminal misappropriation of property.

(h) A sees a ring belonging to Z lying on a table in Z's house. Not venturing to misappropriate the ring immediately for fear of search and detection, A hides the ring in a place where it is highly improbable that it will ever be found by Z, with the intention of taking the ring from the hiding place and selling it when the loss is forgotten. Here A, at the time of first moving the ring, commits theft.

(i) A delivers his watch to Z, a jeweler, to be regulated. Z carries it to his shop. A, not owing to the jeweler any debt for which the jeweler might lawfully detain the watch as a security, enters the shop openly, takes his watch by force out of Z's hand, and carries it away. Here A, though he may have committed criminal trespass and assault, has not committed theft, in as much as what he did was not done dishonestly.

(j) If A owes money to Z for repairing the watch, and if Z retains the watch lawfully as a security for the debt, and A takes the watch out of Z's possession, with the intention of depriving Z of the property as a security for his debt, he commits theft, in as much as he takes it dishonestly.

(k) Again, if A, having pawned his watch to Z, takes it out of Z's possession without Z's consent, not having paid what he borrowed on the watch, he commits theft, though the watch is his own property in as much as he takes it dishonestly.

(l) A takes an article belonging to Z out of Z's possession without Z's consent, with the intention of keeping it until he obtains money from Z as a reward for its restoration. Here A takes dishonestly; A has therefore committed theft.

(m) A, being on friendly terms with Z, goes into Z's library in Z's absence, and takes away a book without Z's express consent for the purpose merely of reading it, and with the intention of returning it. Here, it is probable that A may have conceived that he had Z's implied consent to use Z's book. If this was A's impression, A has not committed theft.

(n) A asks charity from Z's wife. She gives A money, food and clothes, which A knows to belong to Z her husband. Here it is probable that A may conceive that Z's wife is authorised to give away alms. If this was A's impression, A has not committed theft.

(o) A is the paramour of Z's wife. She gives a valuable property, which A knows to belong to her husband Z, and to be such property as she has no authority from Z to give. If A takes the property dishonestly, he commits theft.

(p) A, in good faith, believing property belonging to Z to be A's own property, takes that property out of Z's possession. Here, as A does not take dishonestly, he does not commit theft.

(2) Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both and in case of second or subsequent conviction of any person under this section, he shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years and with fine:

Provided that in cases of theft where the value of the stolen property is less than five thousand rupees, and a person is convicted for the first time, shall upon return of the value of property or restoration of the stolen property, shall be punished with community service.
key_terms: theft
movable property capable of being attached to the earth
moving property in order to taking
dishonest intention as the core of theft
consent express or implied for theft purposes
community service for first-time low-value theft on restitution

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 303 BNS defines theft -- dishonestly intending to take movable property out of someone's possession without their consent, and moving that property in order to effect the taking. The five Explanations clarify what counts as 'movable' (land becomes movable once severed), what counts as 'moving' (even removing an obstacle or inducing an animal to move counts), and that consent can be express or implied. Sixteen illustrations work through edge cases distinguishing theft from criminal breach of trust, criminal misappropriation, and innocent mistake. Punishment is up to three years (enhanced to a mandatory one-to-five-year rigorous-imprisonment band on repeat conviction), with a community-service alternative for first-time low-value theft where the property/its value is restored.
essential_elements: dishonest intention to take movable property
the property is out of the possession of another person
without that person's consent
moving the property in order to effect the taking
exceptions_and_qualifications: A thing attached to the earth is not movable property and so not theft's subject -- until severed (Explanation 1).
Consent may be express or implied, given by the possessor or someone with authority (Explanation 5).
Good-faith belief that the property is one's own, or implied consent genuinely (if mistakenly) believed to exist, negates dishonesty and so negates theft (illustrations (m)-(p)).
First-time conviction for theft of property valued under five thousand rupees draws community service instead of imprisonment, upon return of the property or its value (proviso to sub-section (2)).
breakdown.how_to_read: Work through the Explanations before the illustrations -- 'dishonestly,' 'moves,' and 'consent' are all doing precise technical work here, and the sixteen illustrations exist specifically to map the boundary between theft and its neighbouring offences (criminal breach of trust where property was already entrusted, criminal misappropriation where it was found rather than taken from possession, and no offence at all where genuine good-faith belief negates dishonesty).
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 303 बीएनएस चोरी को परिभाषित करती है — किसी व्यक्ति के कब्जे से, उसकी सहमति के बिना, बेईमानी से चल संपत्ति ले जाने के आशय से, उस संपत्ति को उस लेने के प्रयोजन हेतु हिलाना। पाँच स्पष्टीकरण यह स्पष्ट करते हैं कि 'चल' क्या है (भूमि से पृथक होते ही चल बन जाती है), 'हिलाना' क्या है (बाधा हटाना या पशु को प्रेरित करना भी शामिल), तथा सहमति व्यक्त या विवक्षित हो सकती है। सोलह दृष्टांत चोरी को आपराधिक न्यासभंग, आपराधिक दुर्विनियोग व सद्भावी भूल से अलग करने वाली सीमारेखाओं को स्पष्ट करते हैं। दंड तीन वर्ष तक है (पुनरावृत्ति पर एक-से-पाँच वर्ष के अनिवार्य कठोर कारावास तक बढ़ता है), तथा प्रथम बार के निम्न-मूल्य चोरी हेतु संपत्ति/मूल्य लौटाने पर सामुदायिक सेवा का विकल्प है।
essential_elements_hi: चल संपत्ति बेईमानी से ले जाने का आशय
वह संपत्ति किसी अन्य व्यक्ति के कब्जे में होना
उस व्यक्ति की सहमति के बिना
उस लेने को प्रभावी करने हेतु संपत्ति को हिलाना
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: भूमि से जुड़ी वस्तु चल संपत्ति नहीं है और इसलिए चोरी की विषयवस्तु नहीं — जब तक वह पृथक न कर दी जाए (स्पष्टीकरण 1)।
सहमति व्यक्त या विवक्षित हो सकती है, कब्जाधारी द्वारा या प्राधिकार-प्राप्त किसी व्यक्ति द्वारा दी गई (स्पष्टीकरण 5)।
संपत्ति अपनी स्वयं की होने का सद्भावी विश्वास, या वास्तव में (भले ही भूलवश) विवक्षित सहमति होने का विश्वास, बेईमानी को और इसलिए चोरी को निरस्त करता है (दृष्टांत (म)-(प))।
पाँच हजार रुपये से कम मूल्य की चोरी हेतु प्रथम दोषसिद्धि पर, संपत्ति या उसके मूल्य के लौटाए जाने पर, कारावास के बजाय सामुदायिक सेवा दी जाती है (उपधारा (2) का परंतुक)।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: दृष्टांतों से पहले स्पष्टीकरणों को पढ़ें — 'बेईमानी से', 'हिलाना', और 'सहमति' यहाँ सटीक तकनीकी कार्य कर रहे हैं, और सोलह दृष्टांत विशेष रूप से चोरी और उसके निकटवर्ती अपराधों (जहाँ संपत्ति पहले से न्यासित थी वहाँ आपराधिक न्यासभंग, जहाँ वह कब्जे से लेने के बजाय पाई गई वहाँ आपराधिक दुर्विनियोग, और जहाँ सद्भावी विश्वास बेईमानी को निरस्त करता है वहाँ कोई अपराध नहीं) के बीच की सीमा रेखांकित करने हेतु हैं।

sections.title: Snatching
sections.raw_text:
(1) Theft is snatching if, in order to commit theft, the offender suddenly or quickly or forcibly seizes or secures or grabs or takes away from any person or from his possession any movable property.

(2) Whoever commits snatching, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
key_terms: snatching as a form of theft
sudden quick or forcible seizing to commit theft

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 304 BNS carves 'snatching' out as a distinct, newly-named species of theft -- theft is snatching where the offender suddenly, quickly, or forcibly seizes, secures, grabs, or takes away movable property from a person or their possession, punishable with up to three years' imprisonment plus mandatory fine. This is a new offence category not present in the old Penal Code, created specifically to address chain-snatching and similar sudden-grab thefts.
essential_elements: the underlying conduct satisfies theft (dishonest taking of movable property from possession without consent)
the taking is effected suddenly, quickly, or forcibly -- by seizing, securing, grabbing, or taking away
from a person, or from that person's possession
breakdown.how_to_read: Snatching is defined as a subtype of theft (sub-section (1) begins 'Theft is snatching if...'), so all of Section 303's dishonesty/consent/movable-property requirements still apply -- what distinguishes snatching is purely the suddenness/quickness/forcibleness of the taking, and the fine here is mandatory ('shall also be liable to fine') rather than merely optional as in Section 303's base punishment.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 304 बीएनएस 'झपटमारी' को चोरी की एक पृथक, नव-नामित प्रजाति के रूप में अलग करती है — चोरी झपटमारी है जहाँ अपराधी किसी व्यक्ति से या उसके कब्जे से चल संपत्ति अचानक, त्वरित या बलपूर्वक जब्त, सुरक्षित, छीन या ले जाता है — तीन वर्ष तक के कारावास व अनिवार्य जुर्माने से दंडनीय। यह पुरानी दंड संहिता में अनुपस्थित एक नई अपराध-श्रेणी है, जो विशेष रूप से चेन-स्नैचिंग और इसी प्रकार की अचानक-छीनने वाली चोरियों हेतु बनाई गई है।
essential_elements_hi: अंतर्निहित आचरण चोरी की शर्तें पूरी करता हो (कब्जे से सहमति के बिना चल संपत्ति का बेईमानी से लिया जाना)
वह लेना अचानक, त्वरित या बलपूर्वक प्रभावित किया गया हो — जब्त करके, सुरक्षित करके, छीनकर या ले जाकर
किसी व्यक्ति से, या उस व्यक्ति के कब्जे से
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: झपटमारी को चोरी के एक उपप्रकार के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है (उपधारा (1) 'चोरी झपटमारी है यदि...' से आरंभ होती है), अतः धारा 303 की बेईमानी/सहमति/चल-संपत्ति की सभी अपेक्षाएं अभी भी लागू होती हैं — जो झपटमारी को अलग करता है वह केवल लेने की अचानकता/त्वरितता/बलपूर्वकता है, और यहाँ जुर्माना अनिवार्य है ('जुर्माने के लिए भी दायी होगा') न कि धारा 303 के मूल दंड की भांति केवल वैकल्पिक।

sections.title: Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc.
sections.raw_text:
Whoever commits theft--

(a) in any building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling or used for the custody of property; or

(b) of any means of transport used for the transport of goods or passengers; or

(c) of any article or goods from any means of transport used for the transport of goods or passengers; or

(d) of idol or icon in any place of worship; or

(e) of any property of the Government or of a local authority,

shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
key_terms: theft in a dwelling or property-custody building
theft of or from a means of transport
theft of an idol or icon from a place of worship
theft of government or local-authority property

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 305 BNS enhances theft's punishment for five categories of aggravating context -- theft in a dwelling (building/tent/vessel used as a human dwelling or for property custody), theft of a means of transport, theft of goods/articles from a means of transport, theft of an idol/icon from a place of worship, or theft of Government/local-authority property -- raising the maximum from Section 303's three years to seven years.
essential_elements: the underlying conduct satisfies theft under Section 303

one of five aggravating contexts applies: (a) dwelling/property-custody building/tent/vessel, (b) means of transport itself, (c) goods/articles from a means of transport, (d) idol/icon from a place of worship, or (e) Government/local-authority property
breakdown.how_to_read: This is a sentencing-enhancement provision layered on top of Section 303's base theft definition, structurally similar to how Sections 304-307 each take the core Section 303 definition and attach heavier punishment for specific aggravating circumstances (sudden/forcible taking, dwelling/transport/worship/government property, employment relationship, or preparation for violence).
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 305 बीएनएस पाँच प्रकार की गंभीरताकारी परिस्थितियों हेतु चोरी का दंड बढ़ाती है — निवास स्थान में चोरी (मानव निवास या संपत्ति-अभिरक्षा हेतु प्रयुक्त भवन/तंबू/पोत), परिवहन-साधन की चोरी, परिवहन-साधन से माल/वस्तु की चोरी, पूजा स्थल से मूर्ति/प्रतिमा की चोरी, या सरकार/स्थानीय प्राधिकरण की संपत्ति की चोरी — धारा 303 के तीन वर्ष से बढ़ाकर अधिकतम सात वर्ष तक।
essential_elements_hi: अंतर्निहित आचरण धारा 303 के अंतर्गत चोरी की शर्तें पूरी करता हो

पाँच गंभीरताकारी परिस्थितियों में से एक लागू हो: (क) निवास/संपत्ति-अभिरक्षा भवन/तंबू/पोत, (ख) परिवहन-साधन स्वयं, (ग) परिवहन-साधन से माल/वस्तु, (घ) पूजा स्थल से मूर्ति/प्रतिमा, या (ङ) सरकार/स्थानीय प्राधिकरण की संपत्ति
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: यह धारा 303 की मूल चोरी परिभाषा पर आरोपित एक दंड-वृद्धि उपबंध है, संरचनात्मक रूप से उसी प्रकार जैसे धारा 304-307 में से प्रत्येक धारा 303 की मूल परिभाषा लेकर विशिष्ट गंभीरताकारी परिस्थितियों (अचानक/बलपूर्वक लेना, निवास/परिवहन/पूजा/सरकारी संपत्ति, नियोजन संबंध, या हिंसा की तैयारी) हेतु अधिक कठोर दंड जोड़ती है।

sections.title: Theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master
sections.raw_text: Whoever, being a clerk or servant, or being employed in the capacity of a clerk or servant, commits theft in respect of any property in the possession of his master or employer, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
key_terms: theft by a clerk or servant of the master's property

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 306 BNS enhances theft's punishment where committed by a clerk or servant against property in their master or employer's possession -- a breach-of-trust-adjacent aggravation, punishable with up to seven years' imprisonment plus mandatory fine, matching Section 305's enhanced band.
essential_elements: the accused is a clerk or servant, or employed in the capacity of a clerk or servant
the theft is committed in respect of property in the possession of that person's master or employer
breakdown.how_to_read: The employment relationship itself is the aggravating factor here -- the position of trust a clerk or servant occupies relative to their employer's property justifies punishing theft in that relationship more than twice as severely as ordinary theft under Section 303.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 306 बीएनएस लिपिक या सेवक द्वारा अपने स्वामी या नियोक्ता के कब्जे की संपत्ति के विरुद्ध की गई चोरी हेतु दंड बढ़ाती है — एक न्यासभंग-समीपवर्ती गंभीरता, जो सात वर्ष तक के कारावास व अनिवार्य जुर्माने से दंडनीय है, जो धारा 305 के बढ़े हुए दंड-स्तर से मेल खाती है।
essential_elements_hi: अभियुक्त लिपिक या सेवक हो, अथवा लिपिक या सेवक की हैसियत से नियोजित हो
चोरी उस व्यक्ति के स्वामी या नियोक्ता के कब्जे की संपत्ति के संबंध में की गई हो
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: यहाँ नियोजन संबंध स्वयं गंभीरताकारी कारक है — लिपिक या सेवक अपने नियोक्ता की संपत्ति के संबंध में जिस विश्वास की स्थिति में होता है, वह उस संबंध में चोरी को धारा 303 की साधारण चोरी से दोगुने से अधिक कठोरता से दंडित करने को न्यायोचित ठहराता है।

sections.title: Theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint in order to committing of theft
sections.raw_text:
Whoever commits theft, having made preparation for causing death, or hurt, or restraint, or fear of death, or of hurt, or of restraint, to any person, in order to the committing of such theft, or in order to the effecting of his escape after the committing of such theft, or in order to the retaining of property taken by such theft, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

Illustrations.

(a) A commits theft on property in Z's possession; and while committing this theft, he has a loaded pistol under his garment, having provided this pistol for the purpose of hurting Z in case Z should resist. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

(b) A picks Z's pocket, having posted several of his companions near him, in order that they may restrain Z, if Z should perceive what is passing and should resist, or should attempt to apprehend A. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
key_terms: theft preceded by preparation for causing death hurt or restraint

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 307 BNS is the most severe of the theft-enhancement provisions -- committing theft having prepared in advance to cause (or instil fear of) death, hurt, or restraint, whether to facilitate the theft itself, effect escape afterward, or retain the stolen property, punishable with up to ten years' rigorous imprisonment plus mandatory fine. This sits just below robbery (Section 309) on the violence-proximity spectrum of property offences.
essential_elements: committing theft
having made preparation for causing (or causing fear of) death, hurt, or restraint to a person
that preparation is in order to committing the theft, effecting escape after it, or retaining the stolen property
breakdown.how_to_read: The illustrations clarify this targets preparedness, not actual violence or even an actual threat made -- merely carrying a loaded pistol 'in case' of resistance, or positioning companions 'in order that' they might restrain the victim if needed, suffices even where no violence or threat actually occurs; compare with Section 309's robbery, which requires the violence/fear actually be caused, not merely prepared for.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 307 बीएनएस चोरी-वृद्धि उपबंधों में सर्वाधिक गंभीर है — चोरी करते हुए, उस चोरी को करने हेतु, या चोरी के पश्चात बच निकलने हेतु, या चोरी द्वारा ली गई संपत्ति को रखे रहने हेतु, किसी व्यक्ति की मृत्यु, उपहति या अवरोध कारित करने (या उसका भय उत्पन्न करने) की पूर्व तैयारी करना — दस वर्ष तक के कठोर कारावास व अनिवार्य जुर्माने से दंडनीय। यह संपत्ति-अपराधों की हिंसा-निकटता श्रेणी में डकैती (धारा 309) से ठीक नीचे स्थित है।
essential_elements_hi: चोरी करना
किसी व्यक्ति की मृत्यु, उपहति या अवरोध कारित करने (या उसका भय उत्पन्न करने) की पूर्व तैयारी करना
वह तैयारी चोरी करने, उसके पश्चात बच निकलने, या चुराई गई संपत्ति को रखे रहने हेतु हो
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: दृष्टांत स्पष्ट करते हैं कि यह धारा तैयार-अवस्था को लक्षित करती है, न कि वास्तविक हिंसा या किए गए वास्तविक भय को — प्रतिरोध की स्थिति में उपयोग हेतु भरी पिस्तौल साथ रखना मात्र, या आवश्यकता पड़ने पर पीड़ित को रोकने हेतु साथियों को तैनात करना मात्र, पर्याप्त है भले ही कोई वास्तविक हिंसा या भय न हो; धारा 309 की डकैती से तुलना करें, जिसमें वास्तविक हिंसा/भय कारित होना आवश्यक है, केवल तैयारी पर्याप्त नहीं।

sections.title: Extortion
sections.raw_text:
(1) Whoever intentionally puts any person in fear of any injury to that person, or to any other, and thereby dishonestly induces the person so put in fear to deliver to any person any property, or valuable security or anything signed or sealed which may be converted into a valuable security, commits extortion.

Illustrations.
(a) A threatens to publish a defamatory libel concerning Z unless Z gives him money. He thus induces Z to give him money. A has committed extortion.
(b) A threatens Z that he will keep Z's child in wrongful confinement, unless Z will sign and deliver to A a promissory note binding Z to pay certain monies to A. Z signs and delivers the note. A has committed extortion.
(c) A threatens to send club-men to plough up Z's field unless Z will sign and deliver to B a bond binding Z under a penalty to deliver certain produce to B, and thereby induces Z to sign and deliver the bond. A has committed extortion.
(d) A, by putting Z in fear of grievous hurt, dishonestly induces Z to sign or affix his seal to a blank paper and deliver it to A. Z signs and delivers the paper to A. Here, as the paper so signed may be converted into a valuable security. A has committed extortion.
(e) A threatens Z by sending a message through an electronic device that 'Your child is in my possession, and will be put to death unless you send me one lakh rupees.' A thus induces Z to give him money. A has committed extortion.

(2) Whoever commits extortion shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
(3) Whoever, in order to the committing of extortion, puts any person in fear, or attempts to put any person in fear, of any injury, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
(4) Whoever, in order to the committing of extortion, puts or attempts to put any person in fear of death or of grievous hurt to that person or to any other, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
(5) Whoever commits extortion by putting any person in fear of death or of grievous hurt to that person or to any other, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
(6) Whoever, in order to the committing of extortion, puts or attempts to put any person in fear of an accusation, against that person or any other, of having committed, or attempted to commit, an offence punishable with death or with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
(7) Whoever commits extortion by putting any person in fear of an accusation against that person or any other, of having committed or attempted to commit any offence punishable with death, or with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, or of having attempted to induce any other person to commit such offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
key_terms: extortion
putting a person in fear of injury to dishonestly induce delivery of property
tiered extortion punishment escalating with the severity of the fear used

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 308 BNS opens the 'Of extortion' sub-chapter: extortion is intentionally putting a person in fear of injury (to themselves or another) and thereby dishonestly inducing them to deliver property, a valuable security, or a document convertible into one. The base offence under sub-section (2) carries up to seven years, fine, or both; sub-sections (3)-(7) then layer on a graduated ladder of enhanced punishments depending on whether the fear used (or attempted) is of mere 'any injury', of death or grievous hurt, or of a false accusation of a death/life/ten-year offence, and whether the extortion was merely attempted or actually committed.
essential_elements: intentionally putting a person in fear of any injury to that person or to any other
thereby dishonestly inducing the person so put in fear
to deliver property, valuable security, or a document signed/sealed and convertible into a valuable security
breakdown.how_to_read: Treat sub-section (1) as the master definition and sub-sections (2)-(7) as a punishment ladder keyed to two variables: the type of fear used (generic injury vs. death/grievous hurt vs. false criminal accusation) and whether the offence was completed or only attempted -- the heaviest ten-year bands apply to completed extortion by fear of death/grievous hurt (sub-section 5) and to both attempted and completed extortion by fear of a serious false accusation (sub-sections 6-7), reflecting that a false accusation threat is treated as gravely as a death threat regardless of whether money actually changes hands.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 308 बीएनएस 'उद्दापन' उप-अध्याय का आरंभ करती है: उद्दापन है किसी व्यक्ति को (स्वयं या किसी अन्य को) क्षति का भय जानबूझकर उत्पन्न करना और इस प्रकार उसे बेईमानी से संपत्ति, मूल्यवान प्रतिभूति, या मूल्यवान प्रतिभूति में परिवर्तनीय हस्ताक्षरित/मुद्रांकित वस्तु देने हेतु प्रेरित करना। उपधारा (2) का मूल अपराध सात वर्ष तक, जुर्माना या दोनों से दंडनीय है; उपधारा (3)-(7) फिर इस आधार पर दंड की एक क्रमिक सीढ़ी जोड़ते हैं कि प्रयुक्त (या प्रयत्न किया गया) भय मात्र 'किसी क्षति' का है, या मृत्यु/घोर उपहति का, या मृत्यु/आजीवन कारावास/दस वर्ष के अपराध के झूठे अभियोग का, और क्या उद्दापन केवल प्रयत्न किया गया था या वास्तव में किया गया।
essential_elements_hi: किसी व्यक्ति को (स्वयं या किसी अन्य को) क्षति का भय जानबूझकर उत्पन्न करना
इस प्रकार भयभीत व्यक्ति को बेईमानी से प्रेरित करना
संपत्ति, मूल्यवान प्रतिभूति, या मूल्यवान प्रतिभूति में परिवर्तनीय हस्ताक्षरित/मुद्रांकित दस्तावेज़ देने हेतु
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: उपधारा (1) को मूल परिभाषा मानें और उपधाराएं (2)-(7) को दो चरों पर आधारित दंड-सीढ़ी मानें: प्रयुक्त भय का प्रकार (सामान्य क्षति बनाम मृत्यु/घोर उपहति बनाम गंभीर झूठा आपराधिक अभियोग) और अपराध पूर्ण हुआ या केवल प्रयत्न किया गया — सर्वाधिक कठोर दस-वर्षीय श्रेणियाँ मृत्यु/घोर उपहति के भय द्वारा पूर्ण किए गए उद्दापन (उपधारा 5) तथा गंभीर झूठे अभियोग के भय द्वारा प्रयत्न व पूर्ण दोनों उद्दापन (उपधारा 6-7) पर लागू होती हैं, जो दर्शाता है कि झूठे अभियोग की धमकी को मृत्यु की धमकी जितना ही गंभीर माना जाता है, चाहे धन वास्तव में हाथ बदले या नहीं।

sections.title: Robbery
sections.raw_text:
(1) In all robbery there is either theft or extortion.
(2) Theft is robbery if, in order to the committing of the theft, or in committing the theft, or in carrying away or attempting to carry away property obtained by the theft, the offender, for that end voluntarily causes or attempts to cause to any person death or hurt or wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death or of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint.
(3) Extortion is robbery if the offender, at the time of committing the extortion, is in the presence of the person put in fear, and commits the extortion by putting that person in fear of instant death, of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint to that person or to some other person, and, by so putting in fear, induces the person so put in fear then and there to deliver up the thing extorted.
Explanation.--The offender is said to be present if he is sufficiently near to put the other person in fear of instant death, of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint.

Illustrations.
(a) A holds Z down, and fraudulently takes Z's money and jewels from Z's clothes, without Z's consent. Here A has committed theft, and, in order to the committing of that theft, has voluntarily caused wrongful restraint to Z. A has therefore committed robbery.
(b) A meets Z on the high road, shows a pistol, and demands Z's purse. Z, in consequence, surrenders his purse. Here A has extorted the purse from Z by putting him in fear of instant hurt, and being at the time of committing the extortion in his presence. A has therefore committed robbery.
(c) A meets Z and Z's child on the high road. A takes the child, and threatens to fling it down a precipice, unless Z delivers his purse. Z, in consequence, delivers his purse. Here A has extorted the purse from Z, by causing Z to be in fear of instant hurt to the child who is there present. A has therefore committed robbery on Z.
(d) A obtains property from Z by saying--'Your child is in the hands of my gang, and will be put to death unless you send us ten thousand rupees'. This is extortion, and punishable as such; but it is not robbery, unless Z is put in fear of the instant death of his child.

(4) Whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if the robbery be committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years.
(5) Whoever attempts to commit robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
(6) If any person, in committing or in attempting to commit robbery, voluntarily causes hurt, such person, and any other person jointly concerned in committing or attempting to commit such robbery, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
key_terms: robbery as aggravated theft or aggravated extortion
theft aggravated into robbery by violence or fear of instant harm
extortion aggravated into robbery by the offender's presence and fear of instant harm
enhanced robbery punishment for offences committed on the highway at night
joint liability for hurt voluntarily caused during a robbery

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 309 BNS defines robbery not as a standalone offence but as an aggravated form of theft or extortion: theft becomes robbery when the offender uses or threatens instant violence/restraint to accomplish the taking, make the escape, or keep the property; extortion becomes robbery when the offender is physically present and induces immediate (not future) delivery of the thing extorted through fear of instant harm. Base punishment is up to ten years' rigorous imprisonment plus fine, rising to fourteen years for highway robbery at night; attempt draws up to seven years; and if hurt is voluntarily caused during the robbery or its attempt, every person jointly concerned faces life imprisonment or up to ten years' rigorous imprisonment plus fine.
essential_elements: either theft aggravated by voluntarily causing/attempting death, hurt, or wrongful restraint (or fear of instant versions of these) in order to, during, or in carrying away property from the theft
OR extortion aggravated by the offender's presence and inducing immediate delivery through fear of instant death, hurt, or wrongful restraint
breakdown.how_to_read: The key word distinguishing robbery-via-extortion from plain extortion is 'instant' -- illustration (d) makes this explicit: a ransom demand for future harm to a child already in the demander's custody is extortion but not robbery, because the feared harm is not instant and the offender is not presently threatening the victim face-to-face; contrast illustration (c), where the threat to an immediately present child converts the same basic extortion into robbery.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 309 बीएनएस डकैती को स्वतंत्र अपराध के रूप में नहीं, बल्कि चोरी या उद्दापन के गंभीरतम रूप के रूप में परिभाषित करती है: चोरी डकैती बन जाती है जब अपराधी लेने को पूरा करने, बच निकलने, या संपत्ति रखे रहने हेतु तात्कालिक हिंसा/अवरोध का प्रयोग या धमकी देता है; उद्दापन डकैती बन जाता है जब अपराधी भौतिक रूप से उपस्थित होकर तात्कालिक हानि के भय द्वारा उद्दापित वस्तु का तत्काल प्रदान कराता है। मूल दंड दस वर्ष तक के कठोर कारावास व जुर्माना है, रात्रि में राजमार्ग डकैती हेतु चौदह वर्ष तक बढ़ता है; प्रयत्न सात वर्ष तक दंडनीय है; और यदि डकैती या उसके प्रयत्न में स्वेच्छा से उपहति कारित की जाती है, तो संयुक्त रूप से संलिप्त प्रत्येक व्यक्ति आजीवन कारावास या दस वर्ष तक के कठोर कारावास व जुर्माने का भागी होता है।
essential_elements_hi: या तो चोरी, जो लेने को पूरा करने, करते समय, या चोरी से प्राप्त संपत्ति ले जाने के दौरान स्वेच्छा से मृत्यु/उपहति/सदोष अवरोध कारित करने या उसके प्रयत्न (या इनके तात्कालिक रूप के भय) द्वारा गंभीर हो
अथवा उद्दापन, जो अपराधी की उपस्थिति तथा तात्कालिक मृत्यु/उपहति/सदोष अवरोध के भय द्वारा तत्काल प्रदान कराने से गंभीर हो
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: डकैती-बनाम-उद्दापन को अलग करने वाला मुख्य शब्द 'तात्कालिक' है — दृष्टांत (घ) इसे स्पष्ट करता है: पहले से मांगकर्ता की अभिरक्षा में बच्चे को भविष्य में हानि की धमकी देकर फिरौती मांगना उद्दापन है, डकैती नहीं, क्योंकि आशंकित हानि तात्कालिक नहीं है और अपराधी पीड़ित को प्रत्यक्ष रूप से सामने धमकी नहीं दे रहा; दृष्टांत (ग) से तुलना करें, जहाँ तुरंत उपस्थित बच्चे को धमकी वही मूल उद्दापन को डकैती में बदल देती है।

sections.title: Dacoity
sections.raw_text:
(1) When five or more persons conjointly commit or attempt to commit a robbery, or where the whole number of persons conjointly committing or attempting to commit a robbery, and persons present and aiding such commission or attempt, amount to five or more, every person so committing, attempting or aiding, is said to commit dacoity.
(2) Whoever commits dacoity shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
(3) If any one of five or more persons, who are conjointly committing dacoity, commits murder in so committing dacoity, every one of those persons shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
(4) Whoever makes any preparation for committing dacoity, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
(5) Whoever is one of five or more persons assembled for the purpose of committing dacoity, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
(6) Whoever belongs to a gang of persons associated for the purpose of habitually committing dacoity, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
key_terms: dacoity as robbery by five or more persons
constructive liability of every dacoity participant for a murder committed by any one of them
preparation for committing dacoity as a standalone offence
mere assembly of five or more persons for the purpose of dacoity
belonging to a gang habitually committing dacoity

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 310 BNS defines dacoity purely by headcount: robbery becomes dacoity the moment five or more persons -- whether actually committing, attempting, or merely present and aiding -- are conjointly involved, each of them then said to 'commit dacoity' regardless of their individual role. The section punishes the completed offence (life imprisonment or up to ten years' rigorous imprisonment plus fine), escalates to a mandatory minimum of ten years (up to death or life imprisonment) if any one participant commits murder during the dacoity, and separately criminalises mere preparation, mere assembly of five or more for the purpose, and habitual gang membership -- each an independent offence not requiring the dacoity to have actually occurred.
essential_elements: a robbery (or attempted robbery) that is conjointly committed, OR committed/attempted/aided by a combined total, of five or more persons
breakdown.how_to_read: Sub-section (3) is the sharpest constructive-liability provision in this cluster -- if any one of the five-or-more commits murder while the dacoity is underway, every one of them (not just the actual killer) faces death, life imprisonment, or a mandatory minimum ten years, making group membership during a dacoity itself the source of exposure to a murder-level sentence; sub-sections (4)-(6) then work backward from the completed offence to criminalise the stages leading up to it (preparation, assembly, and habitual gang association) as independently punishable even if no robbery ever actually occurs.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 310 बीएनएस डकैती को विशुद्ध रूप से संख्या-बल के आधार पर परिभाषित करती है: डकैती तब बनती है जब पाँच या अधिक व्यक्ति संयुक्त रूप से डकैती करते या करने का प्रयत्न करते हैं — चाहे वे वास्तव में कर रहे हों, प्रयत्न कर रहे हों, या मात्र उपस्थित रहकर सहायता कर रहे हों — प्रत्येक को 'डकैती करने वाला' माना जाता है चाहे उसकी व्यक्तिगत भूमिका जो भी हो। यह धारा पूर्ण अपराध को दंडित करती है (आजीवन कारावास या दस वर्ष तक कठोर कारावास व जुर्माना), यदि कोई एक भागीदार डकैती के दौरान हत्या करता है तो न्यूनतम दस वर्ष (मृत्युदंड या आजीवन कारावास तक) के अनिवार्य दंड तक बढ़ा देती है, और पृथक रूप से मात्र तैयारी, पाँच या अधिक का मात्र जमावड़ा, तथा आदतन गिरोह-सदस्यता को भी अपराध बनाती है — प्रत्येक एक स्वतंत्र अपराध है जिसके लिए डकैती का वास्तव में घटित होना आवश्यक नहीं।
essential_elements_hi: एक डकैती (या डकैती का प्रयत्न) जो पाँच या अधिक व्यक्तियों द्वारा संयुक्त रूप से की गई हो, या की/प्रयत्न की गई हो/सहायता की गई हो, जिनकी कुल संख्या पाँच या अधिक हो
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: उपधारा (3) इस समूह का सबसे तीक्ष्ण रचनात्मक-दायित्व उपबंध है — यदि पाँच-या-अधिक में से कोई एक डकैती के दौरान हत्या करता है, तो उनमें से प्रत्येक (केवल वास्तविक हत्यारा नहीं) मृत्युदंड, आजीवन कारावास, या अनिवार्य न्यूनतम दस वर्ष का भागी होता है, जिससे डकैती के दौरान समूह-सदस्यता मात्र हत्या-स्तरीय दंड के जोखिम का स्रोत बन जाती है; उपधाराएं (4)-(6) फिर पूर्ण अपराध से पीछे की ओर बढ़ते हुए उसकी ओर ले जाने वाले चरणों (तैयारी, जमावड़ा, और आदतन गिरोह-संबंध) को स्वतंत्र रूप से दंडनीय बनाती हैं, भले ही कोई डकैती वास्तव में कभी न हो।

sections.title: Robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt
sections.raw_text: If, at the time of committing robbery or dacoity, the offender uses any deadly weapon, or causes grievous hurt to any person, or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, the imprisonment with which such offender shall be punished shall not be less than seven years.
key_terms: mandatory minimum sentence for robbery or dacoity involving a deadly weapon or grievous hurt

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 311 BNS sets a mandatory minimum of seven years' imprisonment -- not a ceiling but a floor -- for any offender who, while committing robbery or dacoity, uses a deadly weapon, actually causes grievous hurt, or merely attempts to cause death or grievous hurt, layering a non-negotiable aggravation on top of the ordinary robbery/dacoity sentencing ranges in Sections 309 and 310.
essential_elements: at the time of committing robbery or dacoity
the offender uses any deadly weapon, OR causes grievous hurt to any person, OR attempts to cause death or grievous hurt to any person
breakdown.how_to_read: Note the structural shift from Sections 309-310 (which state maximum/ceiling sentences, 'may extend to') to this section's floor ('shall not be less than') -- it does not create a new offence but instead removes sentencing discretion below seven years once any of its three triggering facts (deadly weapon, actual grievous hurt, or attempted death/grievous hurt) is proved in a robbery or dacoity case.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 311 बीएनएस किसी भी ऐसे अपराधी हेतु सात वर्ष का अनिवार्य न्यूनतम कारावास निर्धारित करती है — यह अधिकतम सीमा नहीं बल्कि एक न्यूनतम सीमा है — जो डकैती या डकैती करते समय कोई घातक हथियार प्रयोग करता है, वास्तव में घोर उपहति कारित करता है, या मात्र मृत्यु या घोर उपहति कारित करने का प्रयत्न करता है, जो धारा 309 व 310 के सामान्य डकैती/लूट दंड-परास पर एक गैर-परक्राम्य गंभीरता आरोपित करती है।
essential_elements_hi: डकैती या लूट करते समय
अपराधी घातक हथियार का प्रयोग करे, अथवा किसी व्यक्ति को घोर उपहति कारित करे, अथवा किसी व्यक्ति को मृत्यु या घोर उपहति कारित करने का प्रयत्न करे
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: धारा 309-310 (जो अधिकतम/ऊपरी सीमा 'तक बढ़ सकता है' बताती हैं) से इस धारा के संरचनात्मक परिवर्तन पर ध्यान दें ('से कम नहीं होगा' की निम्नतम सीमा) — यह कोई नया अपराध नहीं बनाती बल्कि लूट या डकैती के मामले में इसके तीन ट्रिगर तथ्यों (घातक हथियार, वास्तविक घोर उपहति, या मृत्यु/घोर उपहति का प्रयत्न) में से किसी के सिद्ध होते ही सात वर्ष से नीचे का दंड-विवेकाधिकार समाप्त कर देती है।

sections.title: Attempt to commit robbery or dacoity when armed with deadly weapon
sections.raw_text: If, at the time of attempting to commit robbery or dacoity, the offender is armed with any deadly weapon, the imprisonment with which such offender shall be punished shall not be less than seven years.
key_terms: mandatory minimum sentence for attempting robbery or dacoity while armed with a deadly weapon

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 312 BNS mirrors Section 311's mandatory seven-year floor but applies it one stage earlier, to attempted robbery or dacoity: simply being armed with a deadly weapon at the time of the attempt -- without needing to show the weapon was used or that any hurt was caused or attempted -- triggers the same non-negotiable minimum sentence.
essential_elements: at the time of attempting to commit robbery or dacoity
the offender is armed with any deadly weapon
breakdown.how_to_read: Compare directly with Section 311: that section requires the weapon to have been used, or grievous hurt caused or attempted, during a completed-or-attempted robbery/dacoity, whereas this section's trigger is satisfied by mere possession of a deadly weapon during an attempt -- armed presence alone is enough, which is why the two sections are kept separate rather than merged into one.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 312 बीएनएस धारा 311 के अनिवार्य सात-वर्षीय न्यूनतम दंड को एक चरण पहले, लूट या डकैती के प्रयत्न पर लागू करती है: प्रयत्न के समय मात्र घातक हथियार से लैस होना — यह दिखाए बिना कि हथियार का प्रयोग किया गया या कोई उपहति कारित/प्रयत्न की गई — वही गैर-परक्राम्य न्यूनतम दंड उत्पन्न करता है।
essential_elements_hi: लूट या डकैती का प्रयत्न करते समय
अपराधी किसी घातक हथियार से लैस हो
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: धारा 311 से सीधे तुलना करें: उस धारा में पूर्ण-या-प्रयत्न की गई लूट/डकैती के दौरान हथियार का वास्तव में प्रयोग होना, या घोर उपहति कारित/प्रयत्न होना आवश्यक है, जबकि इस धारा का ट्रिगर प्रयत्न के दौरान मात्र घातक हथियार रखने से पूर्ण हो जाता है — केवल सशस्त्र उपस्थिति ही पर्याप्त है, इसीलिए दोनों धाराओं को एक में विलय करने के बजाय पृथक रखा गया है।

sections.title: Punishment for belonging to gang of robbers, etc.
sections.raw_text: Whoever belongs to any gang of persons associated in habitually committing theft or robbery, and not being a gang of dacoits, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
key_terms: belonging to a gang habitually committing theft or robbery that is not a gang of dacoits

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 313 BNS closes the 'Of robbery and dacoity' sub-chapter with a gang-membership offence parallel to Section 310(6)'s dacoity-gang provision, but for the lesser case of gangs habitually committing theft or robbery (explicitly excluding gangs of dacoits, who are punished more heavily under Section 310(6)) -- punishable with up to seven years' rigorous imprisonment plus fine.
essential_elements: belonging to a gang of persons
associated for the purpose of habitually committing theft or robbery
that gang not being a gang of dacoits
breakdown.how_to_read: The express carve-out 'and not being a gang of dacoits' is the operative qualifier -- it prevents this section's seven-year ceiling from overlapping with Section 310(6)'s heavier life-imprisonment-or-ten-years punishment for habitual dacoity-gang membership, so the two provisions sort gang members by the gravity of what their gang habitually does: theft/robbery here, dacoity there.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 313 बीएनएस 'लूट और डकैती' उप-अध्याय को बंद करते हुए धारा 310(6) के डकैत-गिरोह उपबंध के समानांतर एक गिरोह-सदस्यता अपराध प्रस्तुत करती है, किंतु आदतन चोरी या लूट करने वाले गिरोहों (डकैतों के गिरोह को स्पष्ट रूप से छोड़कर, जिन्हें धारा 310(6) के अंतर्गत अधिक कठोरता से दंडित किया जाता है) के निम्नतर मामले हेतु — सात वर्ष तक के कठोर कारावास व जुर्माने से दंडनीय।
essential_elements_hi: व्यक्तियों के किसी गिरोह से संबंधित होना
आदतन चोरी या लूट करने के प्रयोजन हेतु संगठित
वह गिरोह डकैतों का गिरोह न हो
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: स्पष्ट अपवर्जन 'और डकैतों का गिरोह न होना' ही संचालक अर्हता है — यह इस धारा की सात-वर्षीय सीमा को आदतन डकैत-गिरोह सदस्यता हेतु धारा 310(6) के अधिक कठोर आजीवन-कारावास-या-दस-वर्ष दंड से टकराने से रोकता है, इस प्रकार दोनों उपबंध गिरोह सदस्यों को उनके गिरोह के आदतन कृत्य की गंभीरता के अनुसार वर्गीकृत करते हैं: यहाँ चोरी/लूट, वहाँ डकैती।

sections.title: Dishonest misappropriation of property
sections.raw_text:
Whoever dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use any movable property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years and with fine.

Illustrations.
(a) A takes property belonging to Z out of Z's possession, in good faith believing at the time when he takes it, that the property belongs to himself. A is not guilty of theft; but if A, after discovering his mistake, dishonestly appropriates the property to his own use, he is guilty of an offence under this section.
(b) A, being on friendly terms with Z, goes into Z's library in Z's absence, and takes away a book without Z's express consent. Here, if A was under the impression that he had Z's implied consent to take the book for the purpose of reading it, A has not committed theft. But, if A afterwards sells the book for his own benefit, he is guilty of an offence under this section.
(c) A and B, being, joint owners of a horse. A takes the horse out of B's possession, intending to use it. Here, as A has a right to use the horse, he does not dishonestly misappropriate it. But, if A sells the horse and appropriates the whole proceeds to his own use, he is guilty of an offence under this section.

Explanation 1.--A dishonest misappropriation for a time only is a misappropriation within the meaning of this section.

Illustration.
A finds a Government promissory note belonging to Z, bearing a blank endorsement. A, knowing that the note belongs to Z, pledges it with a banker as a security for a loan, intending at a future time to restore it to Z. A has committed an offence under this section.

Explanation 2.--A person who finds property not in the possession of any other person, and takes such property for the purpose of protecting it for, or of restoring it to, the owner, does not take or misappropriate it dishonestly, and is not guilty of an offence; but he is guilty of the offence above defined, if he appropriates it to his own use, when he knows or has the means of discovering the owner, or before he has used reasonable means to discover and give notice to the owner and has kept the property a reasonable time to enable the owner to claim it. What are reasonable means or what is a reasonable time in such a case, is a question of fact. It is not necessary that the finder should know who is the owner of the property, or that any particular person is the owner of it; it is sufficient if, at the time of appropriating it, he does not believe it to be his own property, or in good faith believe that the real owner cannot be found.

Illustrations.
(a) A finds a rupee on the high road, not knowing to whom the rupee belongs, A picks up the rupee. Here A has not committed the offence defined in this section.
(b) A finds a letter on the road, containing a bank-note. From the direction and contents of the letter he learns to whom the note belongs. He appropriates the note. He is guilty of an offence under this section.
(c) A finds a cheque payable to bearer. He can form no conjecture as to the person who has lost the cheque. But the name of the person, who has drawn the cheque, appears. A knows that this person can direct him to the person in whose favour the cheque was drawn. A appropriates the cheque without attempting to discover the owner. He is guilty of an offence under this section.
(d) A sees Z drop his purse with money in it. A picks up the purse with the intention of restoring it to Z, but afterwards appropriates it to his own use. A has committed an offence under this section.
(e) A finds a purse with money, not knowing to whom it belongs; he afterwards discovers that it belongs to Z, and appropriates it to his own use. A is guilty of an offence under this section.
(f) A finds a valuable ring, not knowing to whom it belongs. A sells it immediately without attempting to discover the owner. A is guilty of an offence under this section.
key_terms: dishonest misappropriation of movable property without any prior entrustment
temporary misappropriation still counting as misappropriation
honest-finder exception for property not in anyone's possession
reasonable means and reasonable time to discover the true owner as a question of fact

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 314 BNS opens the 'Of criminal misappropriation of property' sub-chapter: dishonestly misappropriating or converting to one's own use any movable property, punishable with a mandatory minimum six months rising to a maximum of two years, plus fine. Unlike theft (which requires taking property out of someone's possession without consent) or criminal breach of trust (which requires prior entrustment), misappropriation typically begins with innocent or lawful possession -- a mistaken belief, implied permission, joint ownership, or an honest find -- that later turns dishonest once the person appropriates the property to their own use despite knowing it isn't rightfully theirs.
essential_elements: dishonestly misappropriating or converting to one's own use
any movable property
exceptions_and_qualifications: Explanation 2's finder's exception: a person who finds property in no one's possession and takes it to protect or restore it to the owner does not dishonestly misappropriate it, unless they later appropriate it despite knowing or having the means of discovering the owner, or before using reasonable means/time to find and notify the owner.
breakdown.how_to_read: The six illustration sets trace a single recurring pattern worth internalising: lawful or innocent initial possession (mistaken belief of ownership, implied consent, joint ownership, an honest find) is never itself the offence -- the offence crystallises only at the later moment the person, now aware the property isn't truly theirs or that an owner exists/can be found, dishonestly appropriates it anyway; this is why this section is pleaded where theft can't be proved (no non-consensual 'taking' from another's possession) but a later dishonest turn is.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: धारा 314 बीएनएस 'संपत्ति के आपराधिक दुर्विनियोग' उप-अध्याय का आरंभ करती है: किसी चल संपत्ति को बेईमानी से दुर्विनियोजित करना या अपने प्रयोग में परिवर्तित करना, न्यूनतम छह मास से अधिकतम दो वर्ष तक व जुर्माने से दंडनीय। चोरी (जिसमें कब्जे से संपत्ति सहमति के बिना लेना आवश्यक है) या आपराधिक न्यासभंग (जिसमें पूर्व-न्यास आवश्यक है) के विपरीत, दुर्विनियोग सामान्यतः निर्दोष या वैध कब्जे से आरंभ होता है — भूलवश विश्वास, विवक्षित अनुमति, संयुक्त स्वामित्व, या सद्भावी खोज — जो बाद में उस व्यक्ति द्वारा संपत्ति को अपने प्रयोग में लेने पर बेईमानीपूर्ण बन जाता है, जबकि वह जानता है कि वह उसकी वैध संपत्ति नहीं है।
essential_elements_hi: बेईमानी से दुर्विनियोजित करना या अपने प्रयोग में परिवर्तित करना
कोई भी चल संपत्ति
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: स्पष्टीकरण 2 का खोजकर्ता-अपवाद: जो व्यक्ति किसी की भी अभिरक्षा में न रखी संपत्ति पाकर उसे स्वामी हेतु सुरक्षित रखने या लौटाने के लिए लेता है, वह उसे बेईमानी से दुर्विनियोजित नहीं करता, जब तक कि वह बाद में स्वामी को जानते या पता लगाने के साधन होते हुए भी, या स्वामी का पता लगाने व सूचित करने हेतु उचित साधन/समय प्रयोग करने से पहले, उसे अपने प्रयोग में न ले ले।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: छह दृष्टांत-समूह एक बार-बार आने वाले प्रतिमान को दर्शाते हैं, जिसे आत्मसात करना महत्वपूर्ण है: वैध या निर्दोष आरंभिक कब्जा (स्वामित्व का भूलवश विश्वास, विवक्षित सहमति, संयुक्त स्वामित्व, सद्भावी खोज) स्वयं कभी अपराध नहीं है — अपराध केवल उस बाद के क्षण में साकार होता है जब व्यक्ति, अब यह जानते हुए कि संपत्ति वास्तव में उसकी नहीं है या उसका कोई स्वामी मौजूद/पता लगाया जा सकता है, फिर भी उसे बेईमानी से हड़प लेता है; इसीलिए यह धारा वहाँ लगाई जाती है जहाँ चोरी सिद्ध नहीं की जा सकती (किसी अन्य के कब्जे से असहमतिपूर्ण 'लेना' नहीं हुआ) किंतु बाद का बेईमानीपूर्ण मोड़ हुआ है।

sections.title: Dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person at the time of his death
sections.raw_text:
Whoever dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use any property, knowing that such property was in the possession of a deceased person at the time of that person's decease, and has not since been in the possession of any person legally entitled to such possession, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine, and if the offender at the time of such person's decease was employed by him as a clerk or servant, the imprisonment may extend to seven years.

Illustration.
Z dies in possession of furniture and money. His servant A, before the money comes into the possession of any person entitled to such possession, dishonestly misappropriates it. A has committed the offence defined in this section.
key_terms: misappropriating a deceased person's property before it reaches a legally entitled possessor
enhanced punishment where the offender was the deceased's clerk or servant

breakdown.plain_summary: Section 315 BNS is a specialised variant of criminal misappropriation aimed at the vulnerable window immediately after a person's death, before their property has passed into the hands of anyone legally entitled to possess it (heirs, executors, etc.): dishonestly misappropriating such property, knowing it was the deceased's at the time of death and has not since reached a legally entitled possessor, carries up to three years plus fine -- rising to up to seven years if the offender was employed by the deceased as a clerk or servant, mirroring Section 306's enhanced treatment of theft by a servant against a master.
